decisions.reason: Because it builds directly on the firm's wafer and substrate know-how and the firm has its own R&D, management is likely to see enough learning potential to continue improving it rather than withdraw it.

This carrier wafer sits squarely in the firm's established handling and packaging wafer business and matches its stated strategic direction, so absorptive capacity for further refinement is very strong.

Although more advanced and probably still market-building, the copper interposer glass wafer remains closely related to the firm's materials and process capabilities, making continuation more likely than exit.
An off-the-shelf brand for glass and quartz wafers is very close to the core business and should be easy for the firm to market and adapt using its existing knowledge base.

Glass-based circuit boards are materially related but commercially and technologically more distant from the firm's narrow established offer, so even with in-house R&D management is more likely to redeploy resources away from this product.
